# Documents in a relational database

`JSONB` lets a column hold a whole document, binary-encoded and indexable, next to ordinary typed
columns. It is the answer to "we need a bit of schemaless data" that does not require a second
database. The SQL is compact once you know half a dozen operators, and SQLAlchemy maps each of
them to Python.

## Reading values out

| SQL | SQLAlchemy | result |
|---|---|---|
| `payload -> 'k'` | `Event.payload["k"]` | jsonb |
| `payload ->> 'k'` | `Event.payload["k"].astext` | text |
| `payload #>> '{a,b}'` | `Event.payload[("a", "b")].astext` | text, nested |
| `(payload ->> 'k')::int` | `Event.payload["k"].as_integer()` | integer |

A missing key comes back as SQL `NULL`, and that matters more than it looks.

## Filtering, and the NULL trap

Containment, `@>`, is the workhorse: it asks whether the document includes a given fragment, and a
GIN index serves it.

```python
select(Event).where(Event.payload.contains({"user": {"plan": "pro"}}))
```

The trap is negation. `payload ->> 'device' != 'web'` silently drops every row that has no
`device` key at all, because `NULL != 'web'` is not true, it is `NULL`. When absence should count
as "not web", say so: `or_(Event.payload["device"].astext != "web", ~Event.payload.has_key("device"))`.

## Arrays become rows

`jsonb_array_elements` turns one row holding an array into one row per element, and from there
`WHERE`, `GROUP BY` and `JOIN` work as usual. In SQLAlchemy the function becomes something you can
put in `FROM` with `.table_valued(...)`, and a join `ON true`, which Postgres evaluates laterally,
once per row:

```python
item = func.jsonb_array_elements(Event.payload["items"]).table_valued(column("value", JSONB))
select(Event.id, item.c.value["sku"].astext).join(item, true())
```

`jsonb_to_recordset` does the same with typed columns instead of one `jsonb` value, which saves
the casts when the elements share a shape.

## Paths and updates

Postgres 12 added the SQL/JSON path language (`$.items[*] ? (@.qty > 1)`), a small query language
that runs inside one document and is a close cousin of `jq`. Updates are operators too: `||`
merges, `-` removes a key, `#-` removes a path, `jsonb_set` writes one, and `RETURNING` sends back
what changed in the same round trip.

::: {.callout-tip}
## When JSONB, when columns

Use columns for anything you filter, join or aggregate on routinely, and JSONB for the long tail:
attributes that differ per row, payloads you store as received, settings. A GIN index with
`jsonb_path_ops` makes containment fast, but no index makes a JSONB key as cheap to query as a
typed column.
:::
